details: Customers have withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, since it reopened after a $6.3 billion crypto heist. The FBI has attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers. This incident, potentially the largest financial theft in history, has heightened concerns about the security of digital assets and contributed to declines in Bitcoin and Ethereum prices. Binance has stated its commitment to fully cover the losses incurred by users.
title: Binance Faces Billions in Outflows Post-$6.3B Hack

details: The upcoming U.S. midterm elections on November 3, 2026, are a critical event for both financial and cryptocurrency markets. The election outcomes could significantly influence economic policies and the future regulatory environment for digital assets. Historically, Bitcoin has shown a pattern of price declines around previous midterm elections, contributing to current investor uncertainty.
title: US Midterm Elections to Impact Crypto Regulatory Landscape

details: Global markets are exhibiting cautious optimism following reports of diplomatic progress towards a potential U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has led to a 3.2% drop in Brent crude prices. This development is being closely watched as investors also assess the broader geopolitical landscape ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, which could shape the Trump administration's foreign policy and broader economic trends, thereby indirectly influencing market stability and investor risk appetite.
title: Oil Prices Drop on Hopes of US-Iran Deal Amid Midterm Outlook
